quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, must a driver yield to a bicycle coming from the opposite direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Yes. Treat oncoming bicycles the same as oncoming vehicles. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. Only turn when the intersection is clear of all traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Using safe strategies to prevent crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means changing your driving to match weather, how you feel, and how other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians act around you.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to safely return to your lane.

questions.question: What can you do on a road with a broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross it to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before turning.
When traffic moves to the right.
When traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left and there is no sign blocking the turn. Do not turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles traveling straight. You can only turn when it is safe and does not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, must drivers always stop for a stopped school bus?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Yes. Always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: On roadways, what are bicycles considered?
questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly return to the road when it is safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly return to the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road right away. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually turn back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Can drivers park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicap access aisles. These aisles must stay clear for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same way as on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, how far back should you drive?

options.text: Closer than you would behind a regular car.
Farther than you would behind a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Drive farther behind large trucks because they have bigger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle its own full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle its own full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full vehicles with the same road rights as other vehicles. They need a complete lane to move safely. Do not share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your path.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to let you pass safely.
Drive close to parked cars to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your path.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start moving their car without seeing you.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs show construction, maintenance, and emergency work areas.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Use your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Oncoming cars may look slower than they really are. Always check that you have enough space to change lanes safely before passing. If you are unsure, wait until the car passes and you have clear space.

questions.question: Safe passing on a two-way, two-lane street requires:

options.text: You can see the road ahead clearly.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
Your car can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You need all three things to pass safely: clear view of the road ahead, ability to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and a car fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is correct?

options.text: You only need to look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This makes sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at an intersection with multiple lanes, and traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Slowly move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they are leaving a divided roadway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. During the day it looks like a solid orange triangle. At night it appears as a hollow red triangle.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful when turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with the rain, making the road very slippery.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is letting out children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: It is illegal to follow within ____ of an emergency vehicle responding to an emergency.
questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: Make room for ambulances, fire trucks, police cars, and other emergency vehicles. It is illegal to follow within 500 feet of any emergency vehicle using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near any curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a crash.
